children: Dalian iron ore futures fell for a third straight session on Thursday, as rising raw material costs deepened losses at steel mills, outweighing support from higher maritime freight rates and stronger steel exports.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
was down 0.28% at 715 yuan ($106.43) a metric ton, as of 0156 GMT. The contract hit its lowest since August 24 earlier in the day.
The benchmark October iron ore (SZZFV6) on the Singapore Exchange was 1.04% higher at $98.3 a ton.

The average cost of hot iron and steel billets at mainstream mills in Tangshan has risen sharply this week, pushing average losses to more than 100 yuan a ton, according to data from consultancy Mysteel.
Maritime freight rates remained elevated, providing cost support, but the market otherwise lacked a clear short-term direction, analysts from Chinese broker GF Futures said in a note.
Freight rates on major routes to China rose on Wednesday, Mysteel data showed. Higher freight rates tend to support seaborne iron ore prices.

China's total steel exports rose 7.8% week-on-week to 2.55 million tons in the week to August 31, marking the third straight weekly increase and the highest level in nearly eight weeks, Mysteel data showed. On a yearly basis, exports were up 23.9%.
